title: Safe Infant Sleep
objectives: Put baby down safely for naps and at night
Set up a safe sleep space
Know what to keep out of the crib
steps: Place baby on their back for every sleep, naps and at night.
Use a firm, flat sleep surface that is not at an angle or inclined, covered by a fitted sheet.
Keep soft bedding out of the sleep area: no blankets, pillows, bumper pads or soft toys.
Keep baby's crib or bassinet in the room where you sleep, ideally until baby is at least 6 months old.
Do not cover baby's head, and do not let baby get too hot.
Offer a pacifier at nap time and bedtime. If baby is breastfed, you may want to wait until breastfeeding is well established.
source_title: CDC: Providing Care for Babies to Sleep Safely
related_task: Put baby down for a nap
disclaimer: Based on CDC guidance. Not medical advice.

questions.prompt: You are putting baby down for a short daytime nap. How should baby be placed?
options: On their side, so they can see the room
On their back, the same as at night
On their tummy, because naps are short
Any position is fine during the day
questions.explanation: Babies are placed on their back for all sleep times, naps and at night.

questions.prompt: Which sleep space follows the guidance?
options: A firm, flat mattress covered by a fitted sheet, with nothing else on it
A firm mattress with a pillow for comfort
A mattress raised at an angle with a rolled blanket
A crib with bumper pads and a favorite soft toy
questions.explanation: The sleep surface is firm, flat and not inclined, covered by a fitted sheet. Blankets, pillows, bumper pads and soft toys stay out.

questions.prompt: Where should baby's crib or bassinet be?
options: In a separate room from the first night
In the living room, near the TV
Wherever it is warmest in the home
In the room where you sleep, ideally until baby is at least 6 months old
questions.explanation: The guidance is to keep baby's sleep area in the same room where you sleep, ideally until baby is at least 6 months old.

questions.prompt: Which of these should you avoid when baby sleeps?
options: Using a fitted sheet on the mattress
questions.explanation: Do not cover baby's head or let baby get too hot. A pacifier, a fitted sheet and back sleeping are all part of the guidance.
